reading.body:
DFW35 occupies 70,000 square feet of technical space in Richardson, Texas. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this campus, so no IT load, rack count, or accelerator estimate can be derived. Without a power number, the campus cannot be ranked among the 13 Texas facilities that have published capacity figures, and it falls outside the 389 MW total this site has compiled for the state.

The three certifications on record qualify the campus to host payment-card workloads under PCI DSS, to operate an audited information-security management system under ISO 27001, and to demonstrate process-quality standards under ISO 9001. None of those certifications speak to power density, redundancy tier, or AI-specific infrastructure requirements. Which tenants or workload types are actually present is not published.

Texas has 133 mapped facilities in this site's index, making it one of the more densely mapped states in the dataset, yet only 13 of those facilities have published a megawatt figure. DFW35 is among the 120 that have not. For a reader evaluating AI training or large-scale inference capacity, the absence of a power specification is the most important fact about this campus: floor space alone does not establish whether the building can support the sustained, high-density electrical loads that AI workloads require.
